original_question: If one polynomial in a mating is held fixed and the other varies continuously, does the resulting rational map vary continuously? Equivalently, is the mating operation a continuous function of two polynomial variables?
target_in_paper: The draft is targeting §2, "Quasiconformal Surgery," specifically Question 3 on the continuity of mating; this paper is a problem list, so the nearest official formulation is that numbered question rather than a conjecture/proposition/theorem. ([web.pdx.edu](https://web.pdx.edu/~veerman/bielefeld.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the paper's exact target almost verbatim. In §2 the paper asks: if one polynomial is held fixed and the other is varied continuously, does the resulting rational function vary continuously? It immediately restates this as asking whether mating is a continuous function of two variables. ([web.pdx.edu](https://web.pdx.edu/~veerman/bielefeld.pdf))
missing_details: The question is about the specific topological mating construction described immediately beforehand: two monic complex polynomials of the same degree are glued along their circles at infinity, and external rays are collapsed. ([web.pdx.edu](https://web.pdx.edu/~veerman/bielefeld.pdf))
The common degree condition is implicit in the paper's setup and should be stated in a stand-alone version. ([web.pdx.edu](https://web.pdx.edu/~veerman/bielefeld.pdf))
The output is implicitly a rational function of that same degree, not an arbitrary map. ([web.pdx.edu](https://web.pdx.edu/~veerman/bielefeld.pdf))

The domain should be understood as those pairs for which the mating is actually realized by a rational function; Question 1 immediately before Question 3 shows that not every mating is known to do so. ([web.pdx.edu](https://web.pdx.edu/~veerman/bielefeld.pdf))

The paper leaves the topology implicit; for a self-contained formulation one should specify continuous variation in the coefficient topology on monic degree-d polynomials and continuity of the resulting rational map up to Möbius conjugacy (or in moduli space). This clarifies, rather than changes, the paper's intent. ([web.pdx.edu](https://web.pdx.edu/~veerman/bielefeld.pdf))

No connected-Julia-set, postcritically finite, or quadratic-only hypothesis is stated for this mating question itself; those assumptions belong to nearby but different questions and should not be imported. ([web.pdx.edu](https://web.pdx.edu/~veerman/bielefeld.pdf))
refined_question: Fix a common degree d and consider the topological mating of two monic complex polynomials P and Q of degree d, formed by gluing their dynamical disks along the circle at infinity and collapsing external rays, whenever this quotient is realized by a degree-d rational map. Is the resulting rational map, viewed up to Möbius conjugacy, continuous as a function of the pair (P,Q) in the coefficient topology?
equivalent_formulation: If one monic complex polynomial of degree d is held fixed and the other varies continuously, does the degree-d rational map obtained by mating vary continuously (up to Möbius conjugacy)?
justification: This is the narrowest paper-faithful sharpening of your draft. The paper's exact wording is §2, Question 3, and the only essential hidden context comes from the preceding mating setup in the same section: the inputs are two monic polynomials of the same degree, the operation is the topological mating construction, and the intended output is a rational function of that degree. Question 1 immediately before Question 3 shows that existence of a rational realization is itself a separate issue, so the continuity question should be phrased on the domain where the mating is realized by a rational map. The later connectedness/local-connectivity assumptions on page 4 belong to tuning, not mating, so adding them would drift away from the paper's actual scope. ([web.pdx.edu](https://web.pdx.edu/~veerman/bielefeld.pdf))
